title: Compact diagnostic heatmap + progressive-install checklist for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers installing Redwood Private often hit two classes of friction: (1) unclear network bottlenecks when nodes show degraded connectivity, and (2) overwhelming long-install guides that don't surface quick remediation. Goal: Ship a compact visual asset bundle that can be embedded in the Console installer flow and in docs/CLI outputs. The bundle includes: a lightweight network "diagnostic heatmap" (small PNG/SVG + animated GIF demo) that visualizes node-level latency/packet-loss hotspots, a progressive-install checklist micro-UI (fits in a 3-4 step panel), and preflight/upgrade UI mockups that surface inline remediation hints and a rollback preview. This ticket covers concept exploration, high-fidelity mockups for Console and a compact screenshot set for the Quickstart doc, and annotated handoff files for engineering (HTML/CSS tokens + interaction notes). Constraints: assets must be legible at 320px width for mobile/embedded docs, colorblind-safe palette, and exportable as both static (PNG/SVG) and animated (GIF/WebM) for the troubleshooting guide. Success metrics: +15% fewer support tickets for "installation network" tag in the next quarter, decrease mean time to resolution (MTTR) for Private installs by 20% in pilot customers, and positive qualitative feedback from two pilot SE teams.
deliverables: Compact diagnostic heatmap (SVG + 320px PNG) with 3 severity tiers and tooltip overlay specs
Animated GIF demo of heatmap playing through a simulated packet-loss scenario (3s loop)
Console installer micro-panel: progressive-install checklist (3 states: pending/success/warning) with microcopy and error remediation links
Preflight & upgrade UI mocks: inline remediation suggestions, estimated rollback impact, and preflight log pickup button
Documentation screenshot pack: low-bandwidth thumbnails + alt text + cutlines for docs writers
Design tokens and CSS snippets for engineering handoff (color tokens, spacing, micro-interaction timing)
Annotated accessibility notes (keyboard focus order, aria-labels, color contrast table)
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap assets render legibly at 320px width and pass color contrast checks (AA) for all severity states
Checklist micro-panel copy reviewed and approved by PM (Marco Li) and Docs (Sofia Nguyen)
Preflight mocks include at least three distinct remediation suggestions mapped to common failure modes (DNS, firewall, MTU)
Engineering handoff includes CSS tokens and a small interactive spec (focus states + tooltip timing)
Assets uploaded to the design CDN and linked from the Quickstart doc before release-branch cut
updates: 2026-02-28: Ticket created — kickoff meeting scheduled with PM, Eng, and Docs; initial brainstorm produced 3 layout directions (grid, radial, linear) for the heatmap.

2026-03-02: Explored radial vs grid layouts; radial is visually distinctive but less compact at 320px. Decided on a condensed grid with emphasis on link edges for traffic direction (trade-off: slightly less illustrative of topology but better compactness).
2026-03-04: PM review — prioritized DNS/failure remediation content for preflight; added explicit "collect troubleshooting bundle" CTA in preflight mockups per SE request.
2026-03-06: Accessibility pass — swapped red/orange/green palette for colorblind-safe trio (magenta/amber/teal) and tested with contrast tool (passed AA).
2026-03-08: Engineering check-in: confirmed SVG + CSS approach feasible for Console; requested animation as CSS sprite (smaller than GIF) — design to export both GIF and sprite frames.
2026-03-10: Figma handoff frames finalized; uploaded initial PNG/GIF exports to /assets/design/100237. Pending: Docs screenshots and final copy review by Docs lead (Sofia).
decisions: Use a compact grid heatmap representation (4x3 node cells) instead of radial topology to prioritize legibility at small sizes.
Provide both animated GIF and CSS sprite frames for the heatmap; engineering will pick sprite for Console and GIF for docs email templates.
Embed a single-line remediation hint under each preflight check with a "Run diagnostic" CTA that collects a troubleshooting bundle.
Color choices must be colorblind-safe; avoid red-only indicators and rely on iconography + texture patterns for severity distinction.
notes: Pilot ask: include one small variant that shows MTU mismatch as an example failure case used by SEs during customer onboarding sessions.
Edge case: when node count > 12, heatmap should collapse into a summarized bar with "View full diagnostic" link (engineering to handle paginated view).
Docs will request 3 alt-text strings per asset for accessibility and email templates; design to provide concise captions (<= 120 chars).
Follow-up ticket recommended to instrument telemetry when customers click "collect troubleshooting bundle" to measure adoption.
